The general solution to Maxwell's equations is usually difficult to, find. However, analysis of electromagnetic fields requires one to find the general solution without simplifications and assumptions, and our goal is to obtain explicit analytic solutions to Maxwell's equations with the corresponding boundary conditions. This paper researches methods and reports a straightforward mathematical foundation for solving Maxwell's equations in analysis of transverse magnetic (TM) and transverse electric (TE) fields.

articleTitle: Structure of the local Alfven resonance in cylindrical plasmas placed into rippled magnetic field

articleTitle: Wave impedance technique to derive distance from nearby lightning discharges
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. We discuss the results of application of the ELF-VLF wide-band measurement technique for locating nearby lightning discharges. The measurements were performed at Singapore from the field site on board the research vessel. Three field components, namely, vertical electric and two orthogonal horizontal magnetic fields, were digitally recorded and used for the analysis. The distance from the lightning discharge was established using the characteristic frequency dependence of the complex wave impedance spectra pertinent to the nearby lightning discharges of vertical orientation (Korol et al., 1993). The method implies the frequency dependence of the transition range between the static, induction and radiation field components of the wide-band radio signal, similarly to the well-known E-H field technique (Ruhnke, 1971; Kononov et al., 1986). The technique suggested is distinguished by the wide-band measurements that include completely the ELF/VLF range. The horizontal Poynting vector components (Rafalsky et al., 1994) were used to find the source bearing. This technique eliminates an ambiguity in the arrival angle automatically. Simultaneously, a product of the electric and magnetic field components integrated over the pulse duration depends only on coherent portions of a signal. This allows for extraction of the linearly polarised signal, improving the output accuracy of the direction finding. After the source coordinates were established, we used the spectra of the electric and magnetic field components to reconstruct the spectra of the particular current moments of the lightning observed.

articleTitle: Current suppression by external electromagnetic self-detecting structure in galvanomagnetic converters of electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. The paper is devoted to increasing the accuracy of measuring converters (MC) of electromagnetic fields. When designing the galvanomagnetic measuring converters of feed-through power operation on the basis of galvanomagnetic phenomenon in ferromagnetic film, it has been noticed that along with a useful signal proportional to the feed-through power there is a signal proportional to the square of the ratio frequency current flowing though the ferromagnetic film. This undesirable signal is caused by the non-uniformity of the current distribution over the film thickness. A mathematical model of converter has been built. The model of the sensor of the converter of the power flow level is presented as a multilayer dielectric waveguide with layers of finite thickness and permittivity. Between the dielectric layers, a ferromagnetic film of given geometric dimensions and conductivity has been placed.

articleTitle: Pulse signal scattering by object located near the Earth surface
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Mathematical simulation of a pulse signal scattering by an object placed above a dielectric media boundary: for example, air-to-Earth interface, is of interest for a number of electromagnetic and radar problems. Using the Lorenz lemma in the different space regions and combining these results, the authors obtain the integral representation for the field scattered by the object under monochromatic illumination.

articleTitle: Simulation of controllable solid-state structures
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A new class of controllable reflective type antenna arrays is considered, made as microstrip integrated circuits with arbitrary-shape microstrip radiators and controlled elements (crystal diodes). Electromagnetic characteristics of the array are varied by tuning the diode bias voltages. For a digital control possibility, all microstrip radiators are divided into several groups (modules): Each module can be at least in two electromagnetic conditions which are defined by the diodes states (open or closed one). The array controlling is carried out by a microprocessor. The digital array probable states number is proportional to the number of modules and each module allowable conditions number. Digital diffraction reflect-array has a set of microwave radar images whose changing enables one to create so called "intellectual covers" capable to adapt for radar-tracking environment.

articleTitle: Arbitrary shape planar resonator analysis by Galerkin method with edge-accounting basis functions
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A design method for complex resonance frequencies of planar (stripline and slotline) resonators having complicated shape has been developed. The method is based on the solution of surface integro-differential equations by the Galerkin method. The developed method differs from the known ones in using the basis functions defined on the entire surface of the complicated domain. The suggested basis functions take into consideration the behavior of the electromagnetic field near the metal edges of the resonator.

articleTitle: Numerical calculation of the electron distribution function with the goal of simulating a current drive
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The numerical simulation of any kinetic problem associated with auxiliary plasma heating and current drive requires the solution of a Fokker-Planck type equation. One of the main numerical problems of the kinetic equation solution consists of the conservative formulation, which is not so trivial especially for the Coulomb operator. There is a number of tricks designed especially for avoiding the numerical instabilities, but these tricks are not so general and the problem still requests great care. The article presents the results of numerical simulations of some problem associated with producing the current drive by lower hybrid heating. The Fokker-Planck kinetic equation is solved by the finite difference method with the help of the developed FPTM code. We show the results of successful application of the developed code to the one specific problem with the appearance of a plateau on the distribution function in the resonance region.

articleTitle: Electron standing wave resonances in 2-D quantum well and fractional quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We report a theoretical investigation of electron states in an infinitely deep quantum potential well, in which one of the walls has a one-dimensional periodically irregular boundary. It is shown that (1) forbidden gaps in the electron spectrum appear due to standing wave resonances; (2) the fractional quantum Hall effect is explained in the framework of the integer quantum Hall effect theory.

articleTitle: Diffraction of plane waves by a two-impedance wedge in cold plasma
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A wedge is an important conanical structure in diffraction theory. Practically a two-impedance wedge in a cold plasma may be used in modelling the electromagnetic scattering from a variety of large and complex objects. The solution is corrected in comparison with that obtained for the problem in question by Bobrovnikov and Fisanov (1988). In this study the scattered field is represented in the form of a Sommerfeld integral with an unknown spectral function. By using the impedance boundary conditions a nonhomogeneous functional equation is obtained. The solution of the functional equation can be represented in terms of /spl chi/-functions and S integrals. After determining the unknown spectral function in the Sommerfeld integral, the Sommerfeld contour is deformed into the steepest descent paths. During the deformation process the geometrical optics waves and the surface waves contributions are found. Diffraction coefficients are also discussed.

articleTitle: Evolutionary basis and operators of transformation of non-stationary waves in periodic structures
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A new approach to solution of model problems of the linear non-stationary theory of gratings is presented. Its foundation is formed by the operator method in the space of "evolutionary" bases of non-stationary signals.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of some planar microwave gyrotropic structures
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The numerical simulation of different gyrotropic structures plays an increasing role in modern microwave practice. In comparison with the usual analytical/experimental methods known for a number of years, a considerable saving of time and effort combined with some new possibilities for improvement of the analysis before realization of the structures are possible. This new alternative is demonstrated for the case of stripline circulators operating in S-band and below ferromagnetic resonance. The consideration is done with a planar model analysis which offers a reasonable compromise between time consumption and accuracy.

articleTitle: Wave propagation in strongly nonhomogeneous waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Sukhanin (1992, 1994) revealed that the interaction of nonhomogeneities in a strongly non-uniform waveguide is a source of low-frequency waves. The wavelengths of the eigenwave oscillations may exceed the characteristic linear sizes of the structure. Suppose the nonhomogeneous media be a chain of heterogeneities and consist of two materials. Consideration of the oscillation interactions of adjacent heterogeneous media essentially changes the waveguiding and resonance properties and causes the occurrence of a set of low-frequency eigen-oscillations of the chain. To these oscillations there correspond some waves creeping along the nonhomogeneous chain. The heterogeneous poly-dispersity does not significantly affect the low-frequency eigen-oscillations of the chain. The low frequencies of the oscillations are determined by the linear concentration of the nonhomogeneities, the chain period and the oscillation phase shift.

articleTitle: Evolution of a magnetic resonance line under microwave field of high intensity
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The classical description of the electron spin resonance (ESR) phenomenon is based on the known Bloch equation (1946) for a motion of a vector magnetization in a variable magnetic field. In order to study the magnetic relaxation mechanism of ESR phenomena observed in a high intensity microwave field, the authors developed a statistical method of process simulation. Analysis of the calculations of magnetoresonance absorption evolution demonstrates that by taking into account the crystal fields and exchange interaction it is possible to apply this method in the research of more complicated magnetic structures such as ferromagnetics, asperomagnetics, spin-glasses, etc.

articleTitle: Synthesis of the adapted hybrid reflector antennas
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: One approach of solving the synthesis problems of adapted hybrid reflector antennas (HRA) is proposed. It consists of solving the synthesis problem of HRA according to the prescribed directivity pattern (DP) and the problem of forming the deep gap in the DP according to the given direction. The variational formulations for the synthesis problems are used. The mean-square deviation of the given magnitude and the synthesized one is chosen as the optimization criterion.

articleTitle: Diffraction effects in the problem of impedance slit structure emissivity
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The influence of diffraction effects on microwave emission of local objects can be of interest in the problems of remote sensing by passive methods. It is known that the theoretical analysis of similar problems reduces to finding out the diffraction characteristics on these objects. The aim of this paper is to research the diffraction characteristics of electromagnetic waves of a slit structure and to obtain expressions for antenna temperature and emissivity. In this connection a rigorous solution of the diffraction problem of cylindrical electromagnetic waves by an infinite slit in a plane impedance screen is presented. The electromagnetic field of the incident wave is formed by an electric current sheet situated in the far zone of the free half space. Integral equations of the problem are solved by the projection (Galerkin's) method.

articleTitle: Description of the Gaussian beam excited surface wave
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of excitation of surface wave at the interface between two dielectric media is not new. During the last few years the topic concerning the creation of a new type charged particles accelerator, which uses laser radiation has become very popular. For the operation of such devices, the possibility of transforming the beam radiation field into a surface wave field must be investigated. There are several theoretical models describing this problem. We use the Fourier transform technique for the incident and refracted wave. The geometry that is considered is that of a Gaussian beam incident upon the interface separating two dielectric half-spaces. When the angle of incidence of the beam is greater than the total internal reflection angle, the surface wave will appear under the upper medium. We present the Gaussian beam as a integral over the plane wave spectrum. Adding the Fresnel coefficient to the reflection or refraction of the plane waves and using the corresponding boundary conditions, we obtain the field of the reflected or refracted wave.

articleTitle: Transient analysis of transmission lines with time-dependent terminations and general input
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In this paper an exact time-domain solution for the wave equation in lossless TEM transmission lines with time-dependent boundary conditions in the input and output terminals will be presented. First a mathematical closed form time-domain solution for the wave equation in lossless TEM transmissions lines subject to arbitrary terminations will be presented, then this general solution will be specialized for some time dependent resistive terminations. Fundamentals of transient analysis of transmission lines with random inputs such as white noise was also briefly considered in this paper. In the latter situation the results are in the form of some statistical parameters, such as, correlation function, mean, variance and spectral density of the voltage or current stochastic processes, in the line as a function of time and distance.

articleTitle: Application of the wavelet transform to analysis of ultra-wideband processes
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. Ultra-wideband processes take place in nature, physics, and electronics. They appear from transient impacts (shocks) on the medium, electronic devices, etc. In general, their properties are similar to those of the basic wavelet functions. That is why wavelet analysis is suggested for studying ultra-wideband processes which substantially differ from other processes in that they are relatively short and are not quasiperiodic. Examples of ultra-wideband processes are provided from different fields of the wave theory, their mathematical models are constructed, and the requirements the models should meet are specified. Suitable basic functions are suggested for analytical ultra-wideband processes and used for mathematical modeling. The advantage of the wavelet transform over the standard Fourier analysis is demonstrated in the studies of ultra-wideband processes. The examples of practical usage of the technique developed are given.

articleTitle: An algorithm of the method of volume integral equations for analysis of waveguide arrays with protruding dielectric elements
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An algorithm for calculating the characteristics of parallel-plate waveguide arrays with layered dielectric filling and protruding dielectric elements when exciting the waveguides by TEM-waves is proposed. The algorithm is based on the method of volume integral equations for the electric field in the protrusions, and on the method of projection matching the fields on the waveguide aperture. The obtained equations are solved by the method of moments using the piecewise-constant approximation of the field in the protrusion in the longitudinal direction and cosine expansion in each cross section. Results of calculation for a number of structures are presented.

articleTitle: Solution of the problem of excitation of rectangular waveguide section with longitudinally-inhomogeneous medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Discusses the problem of excitation of the considered dielectric structure for longitudinal (oriented along the axis of the waveguide) given currents. The present paper is devoted to building the Green's functions of magnetic and electric types for the sections of rectangular waveguides with three-layer longitudinally-inhomogeneous filling excited by such currents.

articleTitle: Analytical expression transformation for the engineering calculation of parametric absorption effect
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The investigations of the effect of electromagnetic wave energy parametric absorption by the material objects, its consequences and practical applications have been increasing steadily. In the previous works, analytical expressions which took into account the fact that the irradiated object was dielectric, were proposed. In the engineering design, in the case of practical (radar) implementation of the known expressions characterizing the effect of parametric absorption, it became necessary to modify the expressions for a material object constructed of metals (lossy conductors) but not dielectrics. We present the transformed analytical expressions for the engineering calculation of the parametric absorption effect under interaction of an electromagnetic wave and an object made of conducting materials.

articleTitle: On the scattering vibrations in waveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It is known that the existence of eigenvalues of the Laplacian is an essential condition for resonance. That is, if the frequency of the time-harmonic forces belongs to some discrete set on the real axis then the solution of the corresponding non-stationary initial and boundary value problem for the wave equation with a time-harmonic right-hand side increases as t/spl rarr//spl infin/. However, the absence of eigenvalues does not imply the absence of resonances as it has been shown in Wermer (1987) for the case of cylindrical waveguides with constant cross-section. In this paper a class of non-trivial solutions of the homogeneous Dirichlet's boundary value problem for the Helmholtz equation in a two-dimensional waveguide with locally variable cross-section is studied. The feature of these solutions is that they can be not decreasing in infinity. The theorem of non-existence is obtained under fulfilment of one geometrical condition.

articleTitle: Analysis of methods of calculation of electric field in granular material
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The methods of calculation of the electric field in granular materials are analyzed: classical, conformal mappings and breakdown into sections. A conclusion about the necessity of the solution of the Laplace equation for the exact description of the field in a granular material is given.

articleTitle: Eigenoscillations near the arrow-type strip in a channel, 3D effects
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The existence of eigenoscillations near the arrow-type strip in the rectangular channel is proved. It is also proved that the discrete spectrum is infinite and unlimited, and the mode of oscillations for the rectangular strip is found. The numerical evaluation of the oscillation frequencies is carried out using the theory of self-adjoint operators, the "Dirichlet-Neumenn fork", variational methods and analytical methods of waveguide theory.

articleTitle: Investigation of the solutions of the nonlinear antenna synthesis problems
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The antenna synthesis problems according to the prescribed amplitude radiation pattern are considered. The variational statement of the problems is used. The correspond nonlinear Eulerian equations can have a nonunique solution. The derivation of these solutions and an investigation of their properties are carried out using a numerical approach.

articleTitle: Accurate numerical solution of some diffraction problems for axisymmetric thin screens
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We consider a wave diffraction problem associated with an electric dipole radiation in the presence of a finite array of circular perfectly conducting identical disks. An axial dipole is placed on the axis of rotational symmetry. A mathematically and numerically exact solution is obtained. By using the moment method combined with a partial inversion of the problem operator, the problem is reduced to a numerical solution of an infinite matrix equation set of the 2-nd kind. The Fredholm nature of the obtained equations ensures the existence of the unique solution. It is well known that the efficiency of the moment method strongly depends from the correct choice of basic functions. The set of basic functions used turns out to be very convenient one for such class of diffraction problems.

articleTitle: Nonstationary excitation problem solution for a biconical structure consisting of an unclosed cone and isotropic one
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The initial boundary value problem of building a nonstationary Green's function of a perfectly conducting biconical surface consisting of a cone with periodical longitudinal slots and an isotropic one is considered. This geometry can be regarded as a model of a special biconical slot antenna with reflector, or a conical grating with a conical reflection screen. The solution method is based on using the Kontorovich-Lebedev integral transforms and the Rieman-Hilbert method. The analytical solution is derived for some particular cases of the structure.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional beam excitation of a circular dielectric shell
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of the complex source-point beam scattering and absorption by a lossy circular dielectric shell as well as lens-like two-layer cylinder is considered. Both E and H polarizations for inside and outside source locations are treated. An algorithm based on the recurrent formulas for the cylindrical functions with complex arguments has been used. As a result, various scattering patterns as well as the scattered and absorbed power fractions, and directivity were calculated for different shell and cylinder parameters.

articleTitle: Microwave cavity with nonlinear load
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A rigorous solution and numerical results for the problem of excitation of a resonator with nonlinear load are presented. Numerical results are obtained for the excitation by a primary source, whose first or third harmonic in frequency is close to resonance at the fundamental mode H/sub 101/. It was discovered that the amplitude of the third harmonic of the field exceeds the amplitude of the field at the fundamental frequency by 20 to 40 dB.

articleTitle: Arbitrary geometry phased array pattern synthesis procedure
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A universal phased array pattern synthesis procedure is considered. Radiating elements mutual coupling is taken into account by using the array impedance matrix. The procedure is applicable to arbitrary array geometry with N radiators of any arbitrary sort. The required array pattern is specified at M prescribed points with a restricted sidelobe level. The pattern synthesis is considered as a gain maximization process with arbitrary additional conditions. The variational principles are used to obtain the initial approximation, then this solution is corrected using an iterative process. Only the active part of the impedance matrix is needed to be known for solving the problem.

articleTitle: Mathematical models for electromagnetic scattering in R/sup 3/
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We consider the problem of electromagnetic scattering in the infinite connected domain /spl Omega//spl sub/R/sup 3/ with a boundary S. The smooth surface S is assumed to be perfectly conducting. Two cases are considered: (1) S has a finite diameter and S=/spl cup//sup N//sub i=1/S/sub i/, where each connected component S/sub i/, is either a boundary of a limited domain /spl Omega//sub i/ or it is a cut, i.e. a part of the boundary of a limited domain /spl Omega//sub i/ (screen); and (2) S is a k-periodic structure in R/sup 3/, where k=1,2,3, S/spl cap//spl Omega//sub 0/=/spl cup//sup N//sub i=1/S/sub i/, with S/sub i/ described above and /spl Omega//sub 0/, is a cell of the k-periodic structure. A new approach to the scalar and electromagnetic scattering is presented based on the boundary hypersingular integral equations known in mathematics as pseudodifferential equations.

articleTitle: New approach to the wave diffraction by arbitrary dielectric wedge
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of diffraction of an E-polarized plane wave by a dielectric wedge has been treated by a number of authors. In this paper, the integral representations are used for inside and outside solutions. The boundary conditions lead to coupled integral equations of the first kind. In any case, the solution of the integral equation of the 1-st kind leads to an ill-conditioned algebraic system. As a rule, the solution of such a system is connected with any ill-posed problem. The integral transformation is found for the system of integral equations of the 1-st kind and this transformation enables one to obtain a stable solution.

articleTitle: Numerical algorithm for the design of plane junction of two waveguides with arbitrary stepped boundaries of cross-section
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The use of waveguides with nonstandard cross-sections or pieces of such waveguides as fragments of complicated diaphragms or frequency-selective surfaces is now a common practice in microwave engineering. Therefore the general key-building blocks that are oriented on arbitrary waveguide geometry, as well as the specialized key blocks for the fixed geometries are needed when developing the software for exact design of microwave devices. We discuss here the computation of the S-matrixes of a plane junction between two different waveguides with arbitrary stepped boundaries of cross-sections.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Oersted experiments
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An analytical solution is given of the problem of the angle of deviation of the magnetic arrow for want of modification of a distance between it and conductor with a current in the experience of Oersted (1989). The existence of a maximum in the dependence of the indicated angle on the distance is revealed.

articleTitle: The probability distribution of electromagnetic wave intensity formed by its passage through rain fractal model
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The main difficulty in forecasting and calculating the absorption and scattering of electromagnetic waves in rain is the absence of adequate statistical description of rain. The goal of this article is to fill this gap to a certain degree. A fractal model of spatio-temporal chaos of rain intensity is developed for calculating the fluctuations of the electromagnetic wave intensity by its passage through rain.

articleTitle: Successive approach and non-traditional regularization to spectral parameter estimation by least square method
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The peculiarities of a stable least square spectral parameter estimation technique with successive growing model order and adaptive regularization are considered. The advantages of this novel approach are displayed by the results of numerical simulation of complex reflection coefficient spectral analysis for the case of phase distortion due to signal propagation in a waveguide.

articleTitle: Theory of biconical and disk-conical dipole antennas
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Biconical and disk-conical antennas take an important place in the general theory of wide-band antennas. However, in the literature only approximate methods of the solution of integro-differential equations of biconical antennas, which do not enable one to take into account the real geometry of antennas, have been developed. The paper is devoted to the theory of integro-differential equations of such antennas and efficient methods of their solution.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction by a shielded sphere
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: TEM-wave diffraction a by perfectly conducting sphere located between perfectly conducting parallel planes is investigated. The problem is solved by the method of separation of variables and the method of mirror images. It is found a sharp intensification of the Mie effect.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves in millimeter range from canonic scatterers
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. Theoretical investigations on the diffraction of electromagnetic waves from canonical scatterers: a wedge, a semi-plane and a strip, are of current interest for many researchers. It is important to separate two areas of the parameters of the objects under investigation, as they influence the choice of approach to solving the scattering problems. These are the high-frequency (ka/spl Gt/1) and the low-frequency (Ka/spl Lt/1) areas, where k is the wavenumber and a is the characteristic dimension. As a rule, in practical situations in millimeter range the intermediate situation is realized (k/spl sime/1-10). In this situation, the calculations are carried out by approximate methods and determining the criteria of their validity based on the comparison of the theory and the experiment is important. The measurement method of the diffraction field is presented, the characteristics of the scattering from the canonic scatterers and a comparison of the results with the theoretical ones obtained from the physical theory of diffraction are given.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of measurements of dielectric material characteristics using non-sinusoidal signals
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An approximate solution to the problem of reflection of restricted in space transient electromagnetic field from layered lossy dielectric halfspace is described. According to the results obtained an algorithm of determination of dispersion and angular characteristics of dielectric material using the space-time distributions of the reflected field has been derived.

articleTitle: Nonlinear inverse problems of time-harmonic wave suppression in regular waveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper deals with a theoretical and numerical study of nonlinear inverse problems of time-harmonic wave suppression in regular three-dimensional acoustic waveguides. In these problems the field, which is generated by a primary source is given and it is required to suppress it completely or to minimize it by the action of secondary sources. The problems are considered as the minimization problems of some cost functionals. The power radiated to the far zone of the waveguide or the potential energy of the field in some bounded domain of the waveguide are used as these functionals. The coordinates and amplitudes of the secondary antennas play the role of controls. Each of the mentioned functionals is a quadratic function of the complex intensity and, nonconvex general function of the point source coordinates. An efficient numerical method for solution of these problems is developed and some results of numerical experiments are discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic field finding in the source-region of longitudinal slot in a waveguide filled with layered dielectric
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of finding the scattering matrix coefficients of longitudinal slot in a waveguide filled with a layered dielectric is under consideration. The difficulties of representation of the field excited by a longitudinal magnetic current in the source region are discussed. A new way for this representation is proposed, ensuring convergence of the excitation solution.

articleTitle: Object-oriented approach to the development of specialized and general software for microwave CAE & CAD
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problems of computer-aided research of microwave devices have become an independent field of applied microwave CAE over the last 20 years. Under the pressure of growing requirements for the generalization of the design process, they have evolved from algorithmization of particular problem solutions to the creation of multifunctional packages by the microwave device designers. This work is dedicated to creation of problem-oriented electromagnetic design systems by using special C/sup ++/ classes. This is illustrated by considering a program package for filter synthesis and optimization.

articleTitle: Simple approximate formulas for evaluating Sommerfeld type integrals
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The analysis of antennas and scatterers, located in a close proximity to the air/ground interface is concerned with calculation of Sommerfeld improper integrals. This problem has no rigorous solution in a closed form, therefore it is solved either by numerical integration or with the use of approximation. The purpose of the paper is development of more accurate expressions for evaluating the near fields of an infinitesimal electric dipole located over the lossy half-space. Comparative analysis of the numerical results shows that the derived formulas ensure rather high accuracy of the Hertzian potential calculations for the vertical or horizontal electric dipoles over the lossy half-space. The simplicity of the formulas and the absence of numerical integrations makes them convenient for many electromagnetic applications.

articleTitle: Influence of angular correlations on the intensity of scattering from icebergs
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of wave scattering from icebergs has been considered. The angular behavior of the backscattering intensity and angular correlation function for various relations between the wavelength and iceberg height has been investigated. It is shown that the interference pattern arises due to the interaction of the scattered waves. Usage of the observed phenomenon to determine the iceberg height is discussed.

articleTitle: Modern methods for calculation of magnetic field force acting on magnetics
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It is shown, that formulae of the magnetic field action force on a ferromagnetic body, corresponding to various models of magnetization, give the same result while calculating the summary action force of the magnetic field on this body, coinciding with a real force.

articleTitle: Damping of thermal emission interference in oil-water emulsions
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It was discovered from measurements of the thermal radio emission from oil films on water at wavelengths of 0.23 and 0.8 cm that the quasi-periodical dependence of the brightness temperature on the film depth disappears after the first rain. The effect can be related to the phase decorrelation of thermal emission because of scattering on water droplets or on random dielectric heterogeneities in the oil-water emulsion.

articleTitle: Two-stage approach to image compression using wavelet and piecewise-linear transforms
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The information presented in the form of images are becoming more and more popular. Systems like Windows or World Wide Web (WWW) use this method of presentation for most applications. On the other hand, the transmission and storage of huge files containing image data require an enormous memory size and broadband communication. In order to meet these requirements a new approach to image compression, using wavelet and piecewise-linear transforms is presented.

articleTitle: Mathematical method for electromagnetic analysis of two-dimensional waveguide junctions and radiators of complicated shape
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper presents a general algorithm for computing two-dimensional H-plane and E-plane waveguide junctions and antenna radiators having perfectly conducting boundaries. The algorithm is based on the domain product method. The boundary contour is assumed to be a broken line composed of linear segments comparable with the wavelength. The waveguide junctions and waveguide radiators may contain perfectly conducting cylinders. The time dependence is assumed as e/sup j/spl omega/t/. The elements of the scattering matrices S/sub ik/ are calculated with an error not exceeding 0.005.

articleTitle: About the stationary phase points and caustic influence on lateral radiation of antenna systems with radomes
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The influence of re-radiations from a radome inner walls on the lateral radiation of an antenna system is studied. The stationary phase point existence that contribute mainly to the energy of re-radiated beams is determined. The localized, point nature of these sources, increasing the lateral radiation, leads to effective approaches to increasing the noise stability of the antenna system. Further, the envelopes coordinates (caustics) and "controlling" beam re-radiations coming from fixed directions are considered.

articleTitle: Control of electromagnetic radiation and scattering by the usage of smart coatings
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. The development of modern communication and computer systems imposes various requirements on the characteristics of electromagnetic waves radiated by or scattered from the objects to be designed. Currently, two general algorithms exists to solve this problem because of the different requirements imposed on the characteristics of the waves to be radiated or scattered. In this paper, a coating of the object by a thin layer of complicated shape and complex filling is proposed to control its radiation and scattering characteristics. From a mathematical viewpoint, the problem considered can be obviously reduced to solving the wave equations in appropriate regions and matching the solutions in different partial regions by the conjugation conditions. Besides, the additional conditions, such as radiation condition, edge condition, etc., should be satisfied. From a physical viewpoint, our purpose is to find out the material composition that enable the electromagnetic radiation and scattering characteristics to be controlled without changing the geometry of the object, but only changing the shape, thickness and electromagnetic properties of the coating.

articleTitle: Architecture of dielectric bandpass filters with symmetric characteristics
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering from a system of coupled dielectric resonators (DR) placed in a cut off waveguide section has been examined, It has established a common form of characteristic equation for the coupled oscillations, that realizes frequency-symmetrical S matrix parameters. A new structure of the coupling between DRs is indicated as well. Analytical expressions of the power transmission coefficients and experimental investigations of 4 and 5 cylindrical DRs in a microstrip line are given.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous transient conductive half-space: reconstruction of conductivity time-dependence by scattered field
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Inverse problems for a half-space with time-varying conductivity are solved. Determination of conductivity time-dependence after the scattered field is carried out with the assumption of the half-space homogeneity, for a propagating conductivity change and for the transient conductivity which is inhomogeneous in one dimension. Analytical solutions for the conductivity are obtained from integral equations and can be used for the diagnostics problems or for a determination of the conductivity time-dependence providing the required field transformation.

articleTitle: The influence of 3D inhomogeneity of external magnetic field on dispersion properties of low-frequency MHD waves in stellarator
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The report is devoted to studying the effect of three-dimensional (3D) inhomogeneity of the external steady magnetic field B~/sub 0/ on dispersion properties of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves in a stellarator. As far as the helical magnetic field is usually weak as compared with the axial one then we can use a perturbation technique to solve the problem. The inhomogeneity of B~/sub 0/ is shown to result in the weak shift /spl delta//spl omega/ of the MHD waves' eigenfrequency /spl omega/,/spl omega/=/spl omega//sub 0/+/spl delta//spl omega/, where /spl omega//sub 0/ is the eigenfrequency determined in the zeroth approximation.

articleTitle: Some ferrite control components in section of cut-off waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. A comparison analysis of electromagnetic structures-a section of a constant cross-section finite length cut-off waveguide (CCSCW) and a section of a stepped cross-section cut-off waveguide (SCSCW) is presented. A design algorithm of the mentioned structures has been devised. In the present paper, the results of a solution of the problem of rectangular waveguide coupling through such structures are presented. By using the mode matching technique applied for eigenfields at the waveguide junction boundary, the integral equation set has been converted into a matrix equation. Here a Galerkin variational method, whose solution determines the values of the tangential electric field in the openings, is used. The convergence of the obtained solution to the exact one has been proved. Using such a design approach, the structures tunable by magnetic field: ferrite and ferrite-waveguide resonators in CCSCW and SCSCW are considered. A method is presented for calculating the elements of the scattering matrix, the absorption coefficients, the width of the passband, and the resonant frequency of a system consisting of ferrite and ferrite-waveguide resonators. Analytic relationships are derived and graphical dependencies are obtained, which provide an engineering computation to be performed for various designs of ferrite films. The utilization of compound ferrite dielectric plates for the linearization of the field frequency characteristic is shown.

articleTitle: Magnetic field distribution for superconductors with rotational symmetry
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Some studies on the magnetic flux trapped in a hollow superconductor and an applicability of the hollow superconductor for magnetic shielding are reported.

articleTitle: Averaged rough surface backscattering vs. bispectral characteristics of surface shape
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: For an ensemble of wavy surfaces simulating the sea surface, the relation between the averaged resonant backscattering and bispectral surface shape characteristics is studied by means of computer simulation. It is found that for some bispectral characteristics describing waveform peakedness, skewness, ripple concentration, there is a significant correlation to the averaged amplitude of the backscattered signal, the surface spectrum being the same over the ensemble. As an application, a new sea-way model involving, besides to spectral, these bispectral parameters is proposed. This model can describe the manifestation of nonlinear sea-way effects (such as wind-wave interaction, slicks, etc.) in radar images of the sea surface, whereas traditional random phase model (RPM) uses only spectral parameters and thus cannot describe these effects.

articleTitle: Mathematical method of the analysis of "radar-tropospheric waveguide-low flying target over sea surface" radar channel
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We present an approximate method for the analysis of a radar channel consisting of a coastal radar, a tropospheric waveguide and a low flying target over a sea surface. The tropospheric waveguide is formed above the sea due to a number of weather and seasonal-daily factors. In this case the electrical tropospheric parameters near the sea surface essentially differ from a standard one. In 1991-1996, experimental research on the refraction index distribution with height z and electromagnetic field (EM) structure above the Black Sea surface was carried out. Regular measurements were accomplished in a height range from 0 to 30 meters, and separate measurements made up to heights of several kilometers. The experiments prove the possibility of radar identification of ships and low flying targets over the sea surface.

articleTitle: On the one-to-one correspondence of Mueller and Jones matrix formalisms under natural conditions
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It is known that there is a reciprocal correspondence between deterministic Mueller and Jones matrices for nondepolarizing objects. However, in practice, there is a failure to define a Jones matrix corresponding to an experimental Mueller matrix of a deterministic object. The reason of such situation is the presence of experimental errors in the Mueller matrix measurements. A method of finding a deterministic Mueller matrix closest to the initial experimental matrix is offered for which the correspondent Jones matrix can be found. The measurement error influence on the possibility of transforming the measured Mueller matrix to a Jones one for consequent detail analysis is investigated. The corresponding analytical expressions for the transfer of the experimental Mueller matrix to a Jones matrix are presented.

articleTitle: Regularization algorithms for inverse problems in the radiowave probing of the ionospheric plasma
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Inverse problems in radiowave probing of the ionospheric plasma amount to solving integral equations, the right-hand part of which originates from measurements. Therefore, the solutions to such equations are unstable and require the application of regularization algorithms. As an example, we consider the partial reflection technique.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical diffraction tomography
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Tomographical methods of image reconstruction of two-dimensional cross-sections of volumetric objects in the millimeter wavelength band are suggested and considered. Experimental images obtained using antennas of dielectric type and radiation frequency f/spl ap/136 GHz are represented. Volumetric dielectric objects have been taken as objects under investigation. It is shown that in the frequency band under consideration, the images of investigated objects with characteristic dimension A/spl ap/7/spl lambda//spl divide/15/spl lambda/ may be obtained by first-order diffraction tomography method (Born, Rytov or high frequency approximation of the first-order for scattered electromagnetic fields).

articleTitle: Ion motion control by the field of ion-acoustic wave
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Ion motion in the field of an ion-acoustic wave (IAW) is studied. Low-frequency waves are considered. The ions are effectively accelerated by the field of the IAW during a half a period of IAW. When the length of the oscillation is of order of the distance between the initial position of the ions and the surface being processed the interaction of the ions with the surface is possible. The propagation of the IAW is considered in the plasma layer bounded by metal planes. The metal planes are the surfaces being processed. The consideration is carried out for wave which is travelling in a direction parallel to the metal planes and standing in perpendicular direction. The expressions for the electric field of the wave are obtained analytically from Maxwell and quasi-hydrodynamical equations. Using these expressions the ion motion in the structure studied is investigated numerically. The investigation is carried out by using the Runge-Kutta method. It was assumed that initially ions are distributed in the regular intervals in the plasma volume and the initial velocity of ions is zero. The energy and angle distribution of the particle flux on the metal surfaces are obtained for different plasma parameters. The angle and energy distribution of the incident particles can be changed by controlling ion density, wave frequency, wave length and amplitude of the wave. The conditions when the number of particles with large incidence angles and large energy is great enough are determined. Such ion flows can be used for surface processing such as polishing and film deposition.

articleTitle: The matrix formalism for anisotropic and bianisotropic layered medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: Resonant system of selection and absorption of waveguide mode
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Nonsymmetric inhomogeneous lateral expansion of a parallel-plate waveguide containing dielectric layers, a resistive film, and a grating of metallic strips is studied. A propagation constant is found from two-sided equivalent boundary conditions, and scattering coefficients are obtained from the solution of the diffraction problem with the method of moments.

articleTitle: A method for derivation of electric fields in the lower ionosphere from measurements with a partial reflection facility
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The distribution of variations in the effective electron collision frequency was obtained in the 60-66 km altitude range in the lower ionosphere (experimental errors within this altitude range were less than 50%). A technique for estimating the variations in atmospheric electric fields at the lower boundary of the ionosphere was developed using the experimental values of the effective electron collision frequency. From our measurements follows that the electric field E>0.25 V/spl middot/m/sup -1/ in approximately 70% cases under quiet ionospheric and atmospheric conditions. These facts must be taken into account in the investigations of ionospheric processes, meteorological and propagation effects.

articleTitle: Plane wave scattering coefficients for a random surface of arbitrary layered anisotropic dielectric
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The scattering coefficients for the plane harmonic electromagnetic wave with elliptic polarisation that is obliquely incident on the statistically random surface of the layered-inhomogeneous arbitrarily anisotropic half-space are calculated in the first order of the perturbation theory in the case of a small height of the roughness. It is shown that in this approximation the scattering coefficients are expressed through the spectrum of heights of the roughness and through the "external" parameters of the anisotropic half-space with the perfectly uniform surface, i.e. through the plane wave reflection coefficients from the unperturbed boundary and the values of the dielectric tensor components on this surface.

articleTitle: On subsurface radar data processing
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Natural and numeric experiments results show that sophisticated algorithms for subsurface radar system data processing can be developed on the basis of the synthetic aperture algorithm. Nevertheless some modifications of this algorithm have to be done in order to achieve reasonable results in the real media data procession. In this paper the algorithms aimed at the correction of the inverse-matched filter and computation time shortening are presented.

articleTitle: Results of the dynamic radar target characteristics calculations in the decametric wave band
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Presents a mathematical model for a decametric band over-the-horizon-radar and enables one to evaluate the dynamic RCT (radar characteristics of the target) moving over an arbitrary Earth surface. The model basis is a four-beam signal propagation scheme. According to this scheme the electromagnetic field at the observation point is determined as the sum of radio wave fields scattered by the target to the observation point both directly and after reflection from the Earth surface (in various combinations).

articleTitle: On classification of eigenwaves of planar, cylindrical and spherical dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The design and calculation of the characteristics of the integrated optics elements is based on the famous property of a thin layer of dielectric to concentrate the energy of electromagnetic fields in the case when this layer is put on a substrate which has smaller refraction index. A planar dielectric waveguide (a waveguiding layer bounded by parallel planes) is usually considered as a basic element of the integrated optics. It seems promising to consider, in the design of mathematical models of devices of integrated optics, a cylindrical dielectric waveguide (a waveguiding layer enclosed between coaxial cylinders) and a spherical dielectric waveguide (a waveguiding layer enclosed between concentric spheres).

articleTitle: Matching and radiation patterns of waveguide and sectorial horn radiators
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A theoretical and experimental study of the matching of microwave radiators such as the open ends of rectangular waveguides of different dimensions, as well as E- and H-sectorial horns, with free space is carried out. The influence of the matching on these radiators directivity is investigated.

articleTitle: Influence of diffraction effects on radiation characteristics of a wire antenna with finite-size plane and corner reflectors of arbitrary apex angle
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The 3-D radiation problem solution in the far zone of a finite-size corner antenna with an arbitrary aperture angle, excited by an arbitrarily oriented electric dipole, has been obtained by the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UGTD) method. The influence of the diffraction effects on the front-to-back ratio for the main field polarization of corner antennas is analyzed as a function of the apex angle, length and width of the corner faces.

articleTitle: On grounding one class of nonlinear inverse problems of mathematical physics
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The theorems, that ground the statements and numerical methods for solutions of the synthesis problem of the plane aperture shape and amplitude-phase distribution of the field in the aperture for a given power pattern are presented. The numerical examples of synthesis of contour directivity pattern of complicated forms are presented.

articleTitle: Ukrainian radio physical system of seismo-ionospheric monitoring
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper reviews basic ideas, goals and structure of the System of Under-Satellite Ionospheric Sensing (SUIS) which is under development within the framework of research project "Warning". The team of principal developers of this system is with the IRA NAS in Kharkov. It is supposed that SUIS will be based on two sub-systems (SS), namely, monitoring and calibration. The output data of both SS will be first transferred to and processed at the Central Terminal of Ground Data Processing (CTGDP), and further transmitted to the Center of Scientific Data Processing.

articleTitle: Model of signal for digital antenna array with mutual coupling on the basis of face-splitting matrices product
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: When considering the multicoordinate digital antenna arrays (DAA) with mutual coupling of channels there arises a problem of the compact matrix record of the responses of the reception channels. For the solution of the given problem it is proposed to operate with a special type of the product of matrices, called the "face-splitting" and "transposed face-splitting" product (TFSP), respectively. With the aid of the TFSP it is possible to obtain the variant of the analytical model of a two-coordinate DAA with mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Multi-signal studying of seismo-ionospheric interconnections using VLF OmniPAL receiver
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: ELF-VLF measurements aimed at studying seismo-ionospheric effects started at the University of Electro-Communications in Chofu, Tokyo from the beginning of 1997. This work is a further extension of the work of Hayakawa et al. (1996) in which the terminator minimum time method for the searching of earthquake precursors was proposed. The authors found an abnormal shift of the terminator minimum time in the diurnal dependencies of the Omega (Tsushima) VLF station just a few days before the Kobe earthquake (January 17, 1995) and repeated up to the day of the earthquake. In the present work we apply a new processing technique based on wavelet analysis to clarify the hypothesis about the interconnection between an intensification of planetary waves and seismic activity supposed in Hayakawa et al.

articleTitle: The resonance expansion method in surface scattering problems: transmittance of narrow rough-boundary 2D strips
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The influence of inhomogeneities and defects on the transmission properties of waveguides for both quantum and classical waves is a subject of increasing research. We address the interference localization of waves in narrow two-dimensional (2D) surface-corrugated waveguides. The problem stated generally consists of two different rather complicated ones. The first lies in the correct description of the wave interaction with randomly rough surfaces, and the other consists in due consideration of multiple scattering of waveguide modes in searching their localization. The approach most frequently used for taking into account the effect of roughness of the underlying surface on wave propagation is reduced, for the most part, to expansion of the boundary conditions in terms of the power series of the asperity height, and subsequently solving an impedance-type boundary-value statistical problem. We argue that such an approach is unsuitable as applied to wave transfer through narrow surface-corrugated waveguides. We propose an alternative method, derived conformably to the electron transport in rough-bounded quantum wires that eliminates this problem.

articleTitle: Estimating the parameters of spectra in problems of remote radio sounding of near-Earth plasmas
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The accuracy and resolution of remote sensing instruments employing radio-wave techniques can be increased by applying methods of estimation of the model parameters. On the basis of a priori information on the structure of signals, effective computing algorithms for the construction of models of the investigated process are used. The data model is assumed to consist of a limited number of plane waves (oscillations) embedded in noise, and the signal-to-noise ratio q>1. Methods of spectral estimation based on Levinson's, Berg's, Cholesky's and least squares algorithms with the solution of the system of linear equations by Gauss' method are used in the simulations. Applying different methods of autoregressive parameter estimation, computer simulations are conducted at various values of q and for a number of waves (oscillations). The effects of the order of autoregressive models on the results of the evaluation are investigated, as well as the effects of the length of the time series.

articleTitle: Cross-mode modulation effect in Schumann resonances
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The propagation of radio waves through the ionosphere generally results in nonlinear interactions of the electromagnetic field with the plasma, modifying the electrodynamical characteristics of the latter. The question of principal importance for the observation of such effects is sensitivity of the methods and devices applied for the registrations. It is noted that the threshold levels of the external fields for stimulating nonlinear effects in the ionospheric plasma are quite low, varying between 10/sup -5/ and 10/sup -2/ V/m for different types of the effects at different heights. Active experiments with the heating facilities in the USA, the USSR (and later in Russia and Ukraine), and Norway allowed investigating a series of new phenomena in the ionosphere. Other possibilities exist to investigate nonlinear interactions between natural wave fields and the ionosphere, involving no active experiments. Such an approach was realized by the authors in Yampolski et al. (1997), where a cross-modulation effect between the Schumann resonances (SR) and round-the-world HF signals was detected and interpreted. This paper describes an attempt of detecting nonlinear effects in the ELF band alone (4 to 40 Hz) where the Schumann resonance spectrum belongs.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of interaction of shortwave high laser pulses with substance
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The plasma simulation code is described in this article. The two dimensional physical system with r-z symmetry is a basic computation model. The-problem of interaction of shortwave high laser pulses is investigated numerically and is accomplished with the finite particles method applied for numerical computation.

articleTitle: General-purpose computer-controlled polarization state transformer for modern automatic Mueller-polarimeter
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Recently considerable attention is still attracted to creation and development of various schemes of Mueller-polarimeters. However, there are some disadvantages in existing models. In present paper the general-purpose electronically controlled transformer of polarization using electrooptical effect is suggested to utilize it as a main part of modern Mueller-polarimeter. Application of this transformer is shown to give some significant advantages, such as: any polarization state of probing radiation can be realized (generally, the whole Poincare sphere); high speed of measurements (up to 5-10 microsec. per single measurement); possibility of full automatization of Mueller-polarimeter and measurement process; multi-frequency (spectral) measurements (frequency range is limited with other parts of Mueller-polarimeter, in particular, on photodetector); functional elasticity (the possibility of work in main polarimetry measurement regimes: four-polarization method, dual rotating-compensator method; measurement of studied object response to any polarization state of probing radiation; Jones matrix measurement etc.).

articleTitle: Electrodynamic analysis of the eigenmode system of open bilateral slot line
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Presents the problem of wave propagation along a uniform open bilateral slot line. The results obtained by numerical solution provide a way to better understand mode behaviour in lines with a compact cross-section modelling real printed-circuit waveguides.

articleTitle: Development of electromagnetic methods of printed dipole antenna design
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Development of electromagnetic design methods for the radiating devices located in multilayered dielectric structures (MDS), such as microstrip lamellar antennas, printed Yagi antennas, log-periodic dipole antennas, etc., presents an everlasting interest in the modern microwave and millimeter-wave techniques. The paper presents the derivation of the electromagnetic methods for calculating the electric features of a dipole radiator, which is placed in MDS (a basic element of a Yagi antenna). The Feld-Zackson-Vainshtein (1948, 1949, 1988) theory of waveguide excitation is adopted as a basis of the dyadic Green's function derivation.

articleTitle: Radiation of a system of impedance wire antennas in anisotropic medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The studies of linear antennas in anisotropic media are important in such applications as radio communication in space, heating of plasma by high-frequency electromagnetic fields, diagnostics of magnetoactive plasma, electromagnetic compatibility of electronic devices, etc. The publications in these areas concern, basically, single perfectly conducting antennas, which work at the frequencies that result in positive-valued components of the permittivity tensor of the medium. The purpose of the present work is the solution of the problem of excitation of a system of thin impedance wires located in an anisotropic plasma, the permittivity tensor of which can contain not only positive but also negative components.

articleTitle: Model synthesis of efficiently absorbing structures with diffraction gratings
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In this paper we consider certain problems related to the synthesis of the efficiently absorbing structure (perfectly conducting periodic grating covered with a dielectric layer having complex-valued permittivity /spl epsi/). The optimization of absorbing properties of this structure is carried out. As a result, analytical relations between absorbed (reflected) energy and electromagnetic and geometric characteristics of the system under study are derived. These parameters form the input data set in the synthesis problem. Some algorithms for solving relevant inverse problems are suggested.

articleTitle: Remote sensing by VLF using "Absolute OmniPAL". 1. Investigation of short path propagation for possible earthquake precursor detection
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The latest version of the OmniPAL receiver uses GPS to allow drift free logging of the phase and amplitude of phase stable transmissions. Any drift in phase or amplitude can then be attributed to temporal variation of the lower ionosphere. In this paper, the first six weeks of data logged of JG2AS phase and amplitude at three sites in Japan is examined for perturbations. Two sources are identified. Solar flares during daytime and hiss-induced electron precipitation during nighttime. Both of these sources have durations of the order of an hour and, in principle, could be detected by other means and the LF effects allowed for. However, if earthquake precursors have much longer periods (days), the effects of solar flares and electron precipitation can be ignored.

articleTitle: Eigenwaves of bigyrotropic chiral medium under transverse propagation
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We consider here a special case of linear bigyrotropic media that unites both kinds of Faraday chiral media. The joint influence of both electric and magnetic gyrotropy and also chirality parameters on wave propagation is treated. The dispersion equation is considered and a frequency domain analysis is carried out.

articleTitle: Time-domain electromagnetics of waveguide-type open resonators
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: New algorithmic schemes for modeling the problems of linear theory of waveguide discontinuities are presented. Numerical experiment is still the main tool for investigation of the resonant wave scattering phenomena, which are characteristic for such structures. The mathematical approaches employed for such purposes have to satisfy relevant demands for accuracy, efficiency and versatility, and for the ability to be focused on particular details of various practically interesting regimes. The approaches for analyses of transient processes in the waveguide-type open resonators considered here satisfy all these requirements. They rely on the description of the scattering properties of discontinuities in regular waveguides in terms of transform operators related to the "evolutionary basis" of non-stationary signals that are qualitatively the same for all guiding structures. They suppose an application of the analytical regularization technique at key stages of the solving procedure. The approaches developed can be applied to the solution of a wide range of electromagnetic and acoustic boundary value and initial value problems. The class of considered model problems comprises resonant type discontinuities in circular and coaxial waveguides excited by an axisymmetric TE electromagnetic wave.

articleTitle: Self-consistent modeling of high-frequency discharges sustained by azimuthally nonsymmetric surface waves
