publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: VLF scattering from red sprites: vertical columns of ionisation in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Optically, red sprites are observed as clusters of short-lived (/spl sim/50 ms) pinkish-red luminous columns, stretching from /spl sim/40 km to /spl sim/85 km altitude, each about 1 km wide. Red sprite discharges produce columns of ionisation in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide, which can persist for up to /spl sim/100 s at higher altitudes. The ionised columns have been observed through "VLF sprites", perturbations of the phase and/or amplitude of subionospheric VLF transmissions, which can be used to study the electrical properties of the red sprite columns. Previous theoretical studies of red sprite columns have simplified the problem by assuming the columns were of infinite length, or inside a "flat-Earth" waveguide. We present calculations using well-developed VLF propagation methods to describe a finite length sprite inside a realistic Earth-ionosphere waveguide.

articleTitle: Large signal analysis of the modulation response of high speed quantum well lasers
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The main problem for creation of optical communication systems is how quickly the light intensity can be changed under radiation from a laser diode. The improvement of technology of laser structures for switching speed over 30 GHz requires establishing a more accurate relation between authentically measured practical parameters and physical structure of the laser. Peculiarities of application of a dynamic model with partial differential equation for the carrier transport in the SCH region are shown.

articleTitle: Seasonal drift of the global thunderstorms and Schumann resonance frequencies
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We discuss the impact of the seasonal north-south drift of the global thunderstorm centers on the results of observation of the first mode Schumann resonance (SR) frequency. We apply two models of the global thunderstorm distribution. The first is the model of a single compact lightning center. This center is positioned near the evening terminator and has the size of some tens of degrees. At the solstice period of the year, the center shifts southward (during the winter time in the Northern hemisphere) or northward (during the summer). Its diurnal trace coincides with the equator at equinox conditions. The second model is based on the concept of three global thunderstorm centers situated over Africa, Central America and South-East Asia. Seasonal drifts of the centers are pertinent to the model as well.

articleTitle: 4000 km 2.5 Gbit/s single channel laboratory and 245 km 4/spl times/2.5 Gbit/s field transmission experiment of chirped WDM signals over dispersion compensated standard single-mode fibre trunks
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A 4000 km single channel laboratory transmission experiment in a recirculating loop with more than 100 km amplifier spacing and a 245 km field transmission experiment of chirped 4/spl times/2.5 Gbit/s WDM-signals over dispersion compensated standard fibre trunks are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Interpolation for fast efficient excitation modelling technique of open planar circuits and antennas in SDM
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The spectral domain method (SDM) is widely applied to analyse planar microwave circuits but open planar circuit analysis with SDM requires an efficient excitation modelling technique. The excitation modelling technique is very efficient but needs improvement at low frequencies. This paper introduces an interpolation technique to improve the deficiency of excitation modelling at low frequencies.

articleTitle: Effect of mutual excitation of electromagnetic and acoustic waves in a cavity resonator
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The article deals with a detailed analysis of some aspects of solving the problem of acoustic and electromagnetic wave interaction in closed cavities. This necessity for this analysis is caused by the industry demand for more sophisticated and accurate methods of nondestructive material and media testing. Acoustic or electromagnetic waves are generally used for such diagnostics. The joint use of acoustic and electromagnetic waves opens new opportunities in this area.

articleTitle: Approximate versus exact methods in modeling a coaxially excited circular patch antenna
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The fundamental antenna effects of a circular metallic patch antenna on a dielectric substrate backed by a perfectly conducting ground plane and excited by a vertical electrical dipole (VED) are investigated. The solution is numerically accurate in the resonant range due to the sophisticated method used. Resonance conditions are established which maximize the radiation power or efficiency. Criteria are determined for material properties and dimensions, for which surface waves are nearly eliminated and the radiation efficiency approaches 100 percent. Comparison with a magnetic ring model (MRM) for the thin substrates is given.

articleTitle: Integral equations in the problem of diffraction on several parallel impedance strips
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Among the model problems of electromagnetic wave diffraction, an important place is occupied by the problems of diffraction on thin strips. Here, along with the classical problems of diffraction on perfectly conducting surfaces, one can consider the problems, in which the metal strips is not perfect and the real losses are taken into account. The problem of diffraction of a plane time-harmonic electromagnetic wave on a finite number of flat parallel arrays, each of which consists of a finite number of thin strips is considered. The strips are made of real metal with losses that is taken into account by choosing the boundary conditions on their surfaces. The solution of the problem is equivalent to a solution of two boundary value problems.

articleTitle: Optimum design of radar pulses for stealth targets (time domain approach)
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Summary form only given. The principles of an optimum design method of radar nonsinusoidal pulses for stealth targets are presented. First we obtain the time-domain performance of the special absorber, which is used on the target. Using the results of this time-domain approach, we design an optimum pulse figure to maximize the reflected wave energy from the surface of the stealth target. This optimum pulse figure is not necessarily unique. We use a single-layer model of absorbing material, but this method can be generalized for multiple-layer absorbing materials. Also we assume that there is only attenuation during pulse propagation in absorbing material (there is no dispersion). We also show, for the same absorbing material structure and the same reflected energy as used by Mohamed (see IEEE Trans. EMC, vol.37, no.2, 1995), one can use nonsinusoidal radar pulses with larger time-width (narrow-band pulses). It is therefore necessary for time-width of the pulse to be less than the propagation delay time in the absorbing material. Finally, some optimum nonsinusoidal radar pulses are presented for some special applications of stealth targets.

articleTitle: Field calculation of the open magnetic systems by the regularization of Cauchy problem
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The calculation of the scalar magnetic potential distribution of the open electromagnetic systems called a Cauchy problem for the Laplace equation consists in the solution of equation /spl Delta/U=0 under the given boundary conditions, where /spl Delta/ is a differential Laplacian operator. This problem is not correct in the Adamar sense because its solution has no stability. A quasi-transformation method was used for the field solution. It consists in the variation of the differential operators of the Laplacian equation. This variation is carried out introducing the additional differential terms. As a result, an incorrect problem is replaced with a family of correct problems. The further solution has been realized by a numerical finite difference method.

articleTitle: Eigenoscillation near the system of stripes in a channel
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The existence criteria for all types of eigenoscillation modes has been found. The dependence of eigenfrequency on the geometrical and topological parameters of the structure and continuous spectrum of the self-adjoint extension of the Laplace operator has been investigated. The eigenoscillations are classified with the help of the symmetry group.

articleTitle: Forces of interaction between macroscopic objects in the field of electromagnetic wave
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The mechanical action of electromagnetic radiation on material objects (pressure or rotation) is exhibited in many physical phenomena. It plays an important role in the processes inside the stars. It influences the orbits of small particles which move in the space. In the physics of condensed media the electromagnetic (ponderomotive) forces are exhibited in the electrostriction effect. The radiation pressure a plays great role in the interaction of laser pulses with plasma in the laser-heating nuclear fusion machine. It is used for the measurement of the power of microwave and laser radiation. Ponderomotive action of the electromagnetic field on the isolated objects in free space has been investigated previously, both theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Ishimaru parabolic equation: the Languerre invariance of the output time impulses shape
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We show that the approach utilized in Ishimaru's (1977) model to describe a time EM impulse shape behavior in homogeneous nondissipative scattering medium can be extended to inhomogeneous dissipative media. The model extension is based on Omstein-Uhlenbeck dissipative stochastic process application. We have also found the explicit expression for the problem of determining the Green function. The time-dependent term of the Green function is of a Laguerre type for all the considered conditions.

articleTitle: Synthesis of impedance reflector with given scattering characteristics
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of synthesis of an impedance reflector having, at the working wavelength, the same radar cross-section as some perfectly conducting reflector is considered. Analytical expressions for determining the distribution of tensor components of surface impedance for the synthesized reflector are obtained. The influence of the shape of reflector on its frequency-selective properties is investigated.

articleTitle: Numerical solution of Maxwell equations in a two-layered medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper deals with the scattering of an electromagnetic wave by a perfect conductor. The medium exterior to the perfect conductor is constituted by two homogeneous layers with different physical properties. This models for instance the scattering by a submarine antenna. Both media are then the ocean and the air.

articleTitle: A novel approach to the computation of fields inside waveguides and cavities by Fourier series
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: This paper presents a simple and efficient approach to the analysis of waveguides and cavities using Fourier series. This formulation is broad-based and general allowing field solutions to problems in waveguides and cavities with a considerable computational advantage. Numerical results in the form of current distributions are presented to illustrate the theory.

articleTitle: Time and frequency domain algorithms of impulse responses evaluation
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The development of physics and technology of ultrawideband radiation allowed one to radiate into space electromagnetic pulses with a nanosecond duration and power up to 1 GW. The application of such impulses for radar detection of both air and underground objects has been promising. When a received signal is a finite set of digital data, a number of problems concerning the determination of properties of the sounding objects appears. The conclusions drawn form the investigations are summarised.

articleTitle: The method of analysis of the diffraction on step discontinuities
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The new technique of the inversion of a principal part of the integral equation with weighted singularities in the kernel was applied to problem of wave diffraction on a step discontinuities in parallel-plate waveguide. The properties of resulting matrix operator were investigated.

articleTitle: On the structure of the solutions of the antenna synthesis problems according to the prescribed amplitude directivity pattern using the regularization functionals
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It is known, that antenna synthesis problems according to the prescribed amplitude directivity pattern belong to the class of essentially incorrect problems. The absence of demands on the phase directivity pattern under the conditions of the problem should be used as an additional possibility to improve the approximation of the synthesized directivity pattern (DP) to the given one. At the same time, the the nonlinearity of the problem leads to the non-uniqueness of the solutions that complicates the process of numerically searching the solutions. In this report investigations of the quantity and quality characteristics of the existing solutions, based on the methods of functional analysis, are given in the cases of a linear antenna and antennas with plane aperture and their discrete analogy (antenna grids). It turns out that the quantity and the quality of the solutions depend on the value of the electrical size of the aperture, on the value of the space angle (where the DP is given), and on the quality of DP.

articleTitle: Method of solution for the wake field excited by relativistic electron bunch in a dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The dielectric waveguide is one of the simplest slow-wave structures, and therefore an experimental wake field excited by a relativistic electron bunch in a dielectric waveguide is of interest. Zhang et al. (1997) have determined the fields in a flat two dimensional dielectric slow-wave structure. It was revealed that due to multimode interaction in a dielectric slab with a large value of dielectric constant (/spl epsi/=10), the spatial distribution of the wake field is formed by narrow periodically located maxima. The latter propagate along the structure axis with the phase velocity equal to the velocity of the bunch. Such fields can be used both for acceleration of charged particles and for generation of microwaves. Similar wake fields that appear due to propagation of a relativistic electron bunch in a cylindrical dielectric waveguide are investigated in this paper. The problem is solved in the linear approximation for various sets of parameters.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of multiple rectangular aperture irises in rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: It is known that rectangular irises are conventional elements of microwave waveguide circuits. However their application area is limited essentially by their low quality factor. Using multiple aperture irises makes it possible to design circuits with nonconventional features. For example, a design of easily manufactured bandpass filters based on multiple irises with four equal apertures was reported. Frequency response of multiple rectangular irises with different apertures was studied. It appears that such irises have a bandstop feature but this attractive result has been obtained on the basis of an approximate model. So, development of a proper rigorous model is of particular interest. The purpose of this paper is to develop rigorous numerical models of multiple rectangular irises with different apertures and to study their frequency response.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of the E-plane waveguide step
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Using the method of overlapping regions, an electromagnetic model of the rectangular resonant cavity in the E-plane is developed. Based on the theory of transmission lines, scattering matrices of the single ports (of the steps in the E-plane) for cavities of various lengths are calculated. The theoretical results thus obtained agree well with experimental data and can aid the design of a standard for the reflection and transmission coefficients.

articleTitle: Method of asymptotic perturbation of fundamental solution and its application to problems of wave field investigation
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The major points of a new method of calculation of integrals containing the Bessel function are summarized. On the basis of the method of asymptotic perturbations of the fundamental solution the results of the analysis of the fields in a layered structure are obtained. The leading terms of the asymptotic behavior of the fields in the layered structure are obtained.

articleTitle: Technique for determination of RF-magnetic field dependence of the HTS surface impedance by microwave resonators
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The investigations of nonlinear electromagnetic properties of high-temperature superconductors (HTS) in the last years arouse active interest in connection with the prospects of HTS application in various microwave devices (resonators, filters, antennas etc.), with the problems of quality control of these materials, and with the fundamental problems of the physics of superconductors. The nonlinearity of HTS is usually characterized by the dependence of a surface impedance Z/sub s/ on the amplitude of a variable magnetic field H on the HTS surface, i.e. Z/sub s/(H). This dependence is determined by using microwave resonators of various designs. For all resonator types there is a strong inhomogeneity of the field H distribution on the HTS surface. It is shown that the HTS nonlinearity and fields inhomogeneity lead to essential errors in conventional techniques, and a new approach to the problem of diagnostics of nonlinear microwave properties of HTS is advanced.

articleTitle: Plane wave scattering from multilayered resistive-strip grating embedded in a dielectric slab
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An accurate and efficient numerical solution is presented for the two-dimensional electromagnetic wave scattering from multilayered resistive strip gratings embedded in a dielectric slab. Both E- and H-waves are treated. The problem is formulated into a set of integral equations, which is solved by the moment method accompanied by a regularization procedure. The resultant set of linear algebraic equations has the form of Fredholm second kind, and therefore yields stable and accurate numerical solutions. Power distributions computed for several grating parameters are presented. The authors paid special attention to maximizing the absorption into the strips as this analysis is useful in designing electromagnetic wave absorbers.

articleTitle: Plane electromagnetic wave scattering by a spherical inclusion embedded in a lossy film
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The addition theorems are used to treat the problem of the plane electromagnetic wave scattering by a spherical inclusion, embedded in a lossy plane-parallel homogeneous film, covering a lossy half space.

articleTitle: Modeling studies of nonlinear interaction of non-stationary high-power electromagnetic waves with the ionospheric plasma
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The initial set of equations, algorithms for their solution, computer programs, and the results of numerical simulations of nonlinear interaction of non-stationary high-power electromagnetic radiation with plasma in the ionosphere are presented.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a thick diaphragm in parallel-plate waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In this paper we discuss the problem of electromagnetic wave diffraction by a thick inhomogeneous diaphragm in a parallel-plate waveguide. The approach is based on the analytical method of boundary singular integral equations. Similar problems are frequently encountered in the computer-aided design of waveguide circuits. They are normally reduced to the matrix equations by the mode-matching approach. To obtain a stable and accurate algorithm, analytical semi-inversion has been used previously. Unlike this, we develop a discrete mathematical model and numerical algorithm by using the technique proposed by Lipanov (1996).

articleTitle: Permittivity profile synthesis of planar buried waveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The method of finding the permittivity profile of a graded-index single-mode planar waveguide from the given mode parameters is described. For solving this inverse problem the universal mathematical model of the profile is proposed. It has the shape of a double truncated exponential-power function. Each set of function parameters corresponds to a particular distribution of permittivity in the waveguide. The solution of the direct problem by the shift formula method yields the mode parameters of the waveguide. Multiply repeated numerical solution of the direct problem by a special algorithm using the least-square method enables us to select the function parameters for a certain set of mode parameters. As a result of the procedure, the profile function in question is synthesized.

articleTitle: General problem of MHD wave diffraction by MHD inhomogeneity of arbitrary shape
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The general problem of the MHD wave diffraction by an arbitrary inhomogeneity in a plasma is formulated on the basis of integral equations. These equations combine macroscopic equations of field and medium, boundary and initial conditions, in the form of the Volterra equations for non-stationary diffraction, or the integral equations that can be reduced to the Fredholm ones for stationary (time-harmonic) wave diffraction.

articleTitle: Ion motion control by the field of ion-acoustic wave
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: Waveguide section of sequentially included identical elements
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: This paper presents a solution to the problem of symmetric wave diffraction on a set of identical periodical elements in a circular waveguide. Each period includes elementary inhomogeneities such as a ring, radial diaphragm or resistive film, and adjustable magnetodielectric spacers. The period can be equivalently characterized as a four-pole. Analytical formulas for the scattering coefficients are obtained by using matrix polynomial theory. In these formulas, the indices of Mauguin polynomials depend on the number of identical elements in the waveguide.

articleTitle: Nonlinear theory of relativistic microwave electron devices
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The increase of output power is an important task of the theoretical and experimental research of resonant oscillators of millimeter and submillimeter waves (orotron, diffraction action radiation generator, laddertron, ledatron, etc.). It is well known that the application of relativistic voltages for acceleration of electron beams in millimeter wave oscillators allows to obtain high levels of output power of radiation. Dynamic relativistic variation of the electron mass can considerably change the character of the electron-wave interaction process. This effect is essential if the magnetic guide field strength is limited or DC focusing field is nonuniform. In this case the transverse electron-wave interaction and motion of electrons in the transverse direction should be taken into account, and for a theoretical description of the device a multi-dimensional model is applied.

articleTitle: Stochastic model of interaction of electromagnetic waves with random active media
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A model is suggested, which characterizes the transfer of signals in a three-dimensional oscillator neural network with stochastic connections. Each oscillator has the possibility of connection with all the other oscillators. The process of interaction of the signals with oscillators distributed in a spherical region is investigated. The results of modeling show that decreasing the width of the frequency spectra of the signal and oscillator vibrations and their synchronization takes place.

articleTitle: Homogenization theory and impure superconductors
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the homogenization of the Neumann boundary value problem for the stationary and nonstationary Ginzburg-Landau heat equations in a porous medium consisting of a melange of a superconductor and a dielectric with complicated microstructure.

articleTitle: Joint influence of regular and random inhomogeneities on statistical characteristics of waves in layered medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The stationary problem of wave propagation in a layered halfspace with regular and random inhomogeneities is considered. The choice of regular perturbation corresponds to a linear waveguide near the right boundary of the halfspace. Random inhomogeneities are simulated in the framework of the white noise model. We analyze the influence of regular and random inhomogeneities on the probability distribution of the reflection coefficient phase.

articleTitle: Regularization of data processing in six-port reflectometry
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Six-port data processing based on a holographic technique with three reference signals and a corresponding means of generalized residual formal regularization are discussed.

articleTitle: Modelling a spherical patch antenna axisymmetrically excited by a radial probe
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Existing theories for the patch antenna radiation on dielectric layered substrates, especially, for spherical patches are not complete. A mathematically complete theory must have the capability of establishing the existence of an exact solution to the boundary value problem, and result in an algorithm for finding it with a guaranteed accuracy. The method of analytical regularization, exploiting a partial inversion of the basic equations, offers a way of building such a theory. In this paper the problem of modelling a spherical conformal antenna is considered. These antennas are frequently excited by a radial coaxial probe, which can be modelled by an electric dipole located at the surface of the metallic sphere.

articleTitle: H/sub 11/ wave radiation from a circular waveguide with spiral in waveguide aperture
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The radiation of circularly polarized fields is of interest due to its particular properties which are promising for communication systems, antenna arrays, medical equipment, etc. As the H/sub 11/ mode radiation from a circular waveguide is linearly polarized and owing to the circularly polarized radiation of a planar logarithmic spiral, placing the latter in the waveguide aperture is expected to improve the polarization characteristics of radiation. That is why we investigate the radiation of a circular waveguide with a planar spiral in the waveguide aperture. We investigate for the first time the radiation properties of a circular waveguide with a spiral in its aperture using the mode matching method.

articleTitle: Full surface wave analysis of radiation characteristics of tapered slot antennas on dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A full surface wave analysis of the radiation pattern of end-fire tapered slot antennas on dielectric substrates is presented. Numerical results for various geometries and output slot widths of the antennas are given. The results are verified by comparisons with measured patterns for various dielectric substrates and antenna dimensions. It is shown that higher order modes should be taken into account to obtain sufficiently accurate results for wide output slot widths.

articleTitle: Limb-viewing refraction inverse problem in duct case
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The limb-viewing refraction inverse problem for retrieval of refraction index with spherical symmetry distribution in the Earth atmosphere is solved as an ill-posed problem, supposing; that the retrieval height interval is wider than the height interval for ray perigee in which the refraction is given. The problem is solved for the most important case of duct presence.

articleTitle: The influence of 3D inhomogeneity of external magnetic field on dispersion properties of low-frequency MHD waves in stellarator
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: The matrix formalism for anisotropic and bianisotropic layered medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An infinite periodic N-layered structure is considered in this paper. At first the author considers the infinite periodic gyrotropic structure. The translation operator matrix is then discussed as is the dispersion relation.

articleTitle: Method of measuring electromagnetic characteristics of materials
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Measuring electromagnetic characteristics of various media is a starting point in the development of many microwave technologies and instruments. One of the most simple and promising methods is the method of a partially filled waveguide with a shortened end. In a waveguide having a shortened end, a sample which is homogeneous along a certain direction, is placed. Then the wave propagation along such a partially filled waveguide is measured. From such measurements, the sample material characteristics, such as complex permittivity and loss tangent, may be derived.

articleTitle: Is there a physical coherence between the problems of wave scattering from absolutely soft and impedance rough surfaces?
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: For over than thirty years it has been believed that the scattering of waves by a randomly rough surface with sufficiently small elevations runs similarly to the scattering by an ideal (unperturbed) surface but having a random impedance. Based on this belief, many of authors applied a habitual simplifying trick from the very outset of handling the wave scattering problem: they replaced the exact boundary condition by its Taylor expansion in terms of the irregularities height keeping only linear term. Following a thorough analysis the authors conclude that a necessary condition for the replacement of an absolutely soft-wall scattering problem with the corresponding impedance approach is the firm certainty that the physical quantities sought are mainly formed by the natural modes whose wavelengths far exceed the average height of the surface elevations.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian approach to the problem of wave collapse
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Formation of singularities in the wave system within a finite time, or, in the other words, a wave collapse is one of the basic phenomena in nonlinear physics. The collapse plays an essential role in various fields of physics. Intense, localized, high-frequency waves can modify the medium in which they propagate via excitation of low frequency disturbances by their ponderomotive forces, for example. A common feature is that the collapse involves interaction between high and low-frequency waves coupled by nonlinear interactions that cause the refractive index of high-frequency waves to increase with increasing the wave intensity. The resulting tendency to focus into regions of high intensity can then lead to collapse. By using the Hamiltonian formalism for the analysis of stationary solutions, the author proves that the Hamiltonian is limited from below for the fixed plasmon number. This enables conclusions to be made about the possibility of existence of stable solutions.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of dipole arrays
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the electromagnetic analysis of infinite periodic and finite dipole arrays on the basis of the singular integro-differential equations. Linear arrays of parallel wire antennas and two-dimensional planar arrays are considered.

articleTitle: Numerical technique for inverse problems of geometrical optics of inhomogeneous media
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The synthesis of inhomogeneous lenses, the problems of phase tomography of one-dimensional gradient media in geometrical optics approximation, etc., can be reduced to nonlinear integral equations relatively to an unknown function of the index of refraction. These equations have closed-form solutions in a small number of particular cases. A new technique to solve these problems is proposed. According to this technique, we analyze a layered medium instead of an inhomogeneous one. As a result, we have a stepped-law function of the index of refraction variation. It is possible to decrease the difference between the stepped and the continuous-law functions by increasing the number of layers. Three modifications of this technique: ray, phase and combined, are used to investigate inhomogeneous media where the index of refraction is a function of the Cartesian coordinate or radius. The latter two provide the desired accuracy.

articleTitle: Solution of inverse problem for a charge combined with a point-like dipole
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Inverse problems in electrodynamics are not sufficiently advanced though they are of certain theoretical interest and practical implementation. Here we propose a particular inverse problem of electrostatics. It is well known that the field induced by electric charge arbitrarily distributed within a finite area is, in the far-field approximation, equal to the field of a point-like charge and dipole moment. Calculation of the field produced by a given charge or dipole moment is referred to as a direct problem.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic waves in a gyrotropic rod with arbitrary direction of external magnetic field
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Large numbers of publications have been devoted to studying the spectral characteristics of electromagnetic waves in circular material rods. In so doing it was supposed that either the rod was isotropic or the axis of anisotropy or the direction of an external magnetic field coincided with the geometrical axis. In Eremenko and Filipov (1996) and Filipov (1997) the waves in anisotropic and semiconducting rods were investigated assuming arbitrary directions of the mentioned vectors. In practical applications, it is interesting to study the waves in rods made from magnetodielectric materials, whose parameters are described by the components of tensor dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability. In particular, these are ferromagnetic semiconductors combining magnetic ordering and large mobility of carriers, and also anisotropic ferrites. The characteristics of the waves propagating on such rods are obtained from the solutions of the Maxwell equations.

articleTitle: About possible harbingers of earthquakes in characteristics of VLF signals of electromagnetic background
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Information for the forecasting of earthquakes can be obtained by sounding the whole of the ionosphere disturbed by precursors, i.e. by realizing monitoring of the space-time parameters of the ionosphere over a wide range of heights and large areas, that is by using the ionosphere as a detector of events accompanying the earthquake preparation process. Regular measurements of the parameters of VLF-signals along the routes of different orientation and extention, passing near seismoactive regions, and the data of vertical sounding of ionosphere are analyzed.

articleTitle: Detecting quadratic-type nonlinearities of random processes in the presence of additive noise
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of detecting nonlinear effects often arises in investigations of different physical, engineering and other systems. These can be, for example, nonlinear distortions in radio devices, coupling of waves in nonlinear media, or nonlinear mechanisms of their generation. A powerful tool for solving this problem is the use of cumulants or their associated Fourier transforms, known as polyspectra. However, the estimation of cumulants (or polyspectra) of real processes (especially for fairly long realizations) requires considerable computation resources, in particular, RAM. The present paper illustrates the potentials of the so called "1 1/2 D-spectra", /spl Gamma/(/spl omega/), for solving the problem of detecting weak quadratic-type nonlinearities of random processes in the presence of additive noise. This technique is a particular case of the bispectral analysis being, however, it is much easier to use.

articleTitle: Energy fluxes and resonances in waveguides with obstacles
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Semi-analytical approaches to building low cost computer models of elastic wave excitation, propagation and diffraction phenomena related primarily to seismoacoustics and nondestructive testing, are developed. These methods are quite applicable to the electromagnetic wave propagation problems as well. The main features ensuring their high efficiency are outlined. The authors examine how the shape of a crack influenced the reflected field (the scattering cross section, scattering patterns, power redistribution) and the location of the scattering resonances in the complex frequency plane. A possible use of the obtained dependence of the resonance poles against the scatterer shape and size for regularisation of the ill-posed inverse problems is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of coupled cylindrical slot and strip lines based on the Riemann-Hilbert problem method
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of two open coupled metal-dielectric lines is topical for directional couplers, filters, antennas, etc. in so far as accurate models of these structures are indispensable to computer aided design. The presented accurate approach is capable of analyzing the waves in structures composed of two circular cylindrical slot/strip lines (CSlLs/CStLs) which belong to the family of the so-called nonplanar lines. Each CSlL/CStL consists of a circular dielectric rod coated with an infinitely thin metal slotted cylinder so that the longitudinal slot runs in the propagation direction. When the slot opening /spl theta/>/spl pi/, the cylindrical slot line (CSlL) is considered as a cylindrical strip line (CStL). The discrete spectrum modes of some variants of coupled CSlLs/CStLs are discussed.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of radiation of antenna arrays
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of analysis of the directional properties and frequency characteristics of dipole antenna arrays is considered. The influence of a perfectly conducting screen and feeding circuits on the array performance is analyzed. The practical recommendations for the design of high-gain broadband receiving antenna arrays are elaborated.

articleTitle: Improved algorithm based on Rytov approximation for three-dimensional structure determination of biological objects
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: An inverse scattering formulation is developed for large size-low contrast dielectric objects, based on Rytov approximation and optimization techniques for three dimensional (3D) scalar waves, providing an efficient solution to the diffraction tomography problem associated with the imaging of soft tissues in biomedical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Diffraction of electromagnetic waves by gratings with piecewise smooth boundaries
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We consider a boundary value problem for the Helmholtz equation that arises in the mathematical modeling of the scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by infinite perfectly conducting gratings with an arbitrary piecewise-smooth profile of finite size. In the Hilbert space of the square-integrable functions we find the solution of this problem as a potential whose density represents a solution of a weakly singular integral equation.

articleTitle: Ill-posed inverse problems based on Volterra-type equations
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Inverse problems based on Volterra equations are, as a rule, well-posed. But in the case when a function should be retrieved in the range which is wider than the range where the right side of the equation is given, the solution appears an ill-posed inverse problem. A number of physical examples in electromagnetics is given, and it is shown that such inverse problems could be successfully solved on the basis of Tikhonov's method of general discrepancy.

articleTitle: Polarization transformation in irregular circular waveguides with helical corrugation and gyrotropic filling
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: Self-consistent modeling of high-frequency discharges sustained by azimuthally nonsymmetric surface waves
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A self-consistent model of high-frequency generated discharges sustained, under the conditions of an ambipolar diffusion controlled regime, by azimuthally nonsymmetric surface waves (SW) is proposed. The potential SW propagate in cylindrical plasma column surrounded by a dielectric tube. The investigation was carried out for argon plasma. A complete set of relations is formed by the charged particle balance equation, electron energy balance relation, and the equation for the potential of the surface wave electric field. The stationary gas discharge is considered. It is assumed that density variation in the direction of the column axis is small. In this case the set of equations reduces to a set of one-dimensional ordinary differential equations in the radial co-ordinate. The problem is solved numerically. Self consistent radial profiles of electron density, ambipolar velocity of particles, electron temperature and SW electric field potential are obtained.

articleTitle: Unified structure and approach for performing fast transformations and nonlinear operations
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A unified structure for performing fast discrete orthogonal transformations like Fourier, Walsh, Haar, cosine and sine ones and nonlinear operations like scanning window data sorting for order statistic and L-filters is proposed and described. It permits one to implement a wide class of techniques used in signal and image processing applications.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of a displacement of autocorrelated functions processing procedures by incoherent scattering in ionosphere
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The new statistical approach to the analysis of data from incoherent scattering in ionosphere is offered. It consists of accounting for the displacement of values of autocorrelated functions estimation. It is shown that with this approach the error of estimating the temperature of the ionic and electronic ionosphere is reduced considerably.

articleTitle: Determination of size and number density of water droplets by the measurement of intensity of scattered light
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The concentration of water vapour varies with space and time. It is removed from the troposphere due the precipitation of water. The size of condensing nuclei and aerosol particles present in the atmosphere are comparable to the wavelength of visible radiation. According to Mie theory, the scattering properties are the function of size parameter x, refractive index m and the angle of scattering /spl theta/. The light scattered from condensing droplets illuminated by a 5 mw He-Ne laser beam is detected at 45/spl deg/ and 135/spl deg/ simultaneously. The observed ratio of intensities of scattered light is compared with the theoretically calculated value. The method also enables one to determine the number density N and modal size x/sub m/ of water droplets. The effect of ions of water vapour condensation is also studied by this method.

articleTitle: Calculation of atmospheric electricity day trend
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the problems of approximation of the atmospheric electricity daily trend. It is shown that for the approximation of the time trend with a 3 to 4% error, 5 sine harmonics or 10 sine-cosine harmonics are enough. An algorithm is presented based on statistical and spectral methods.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal effect in transverse-magnetized ferromagnetic-metal-on-amplifier magnetooptical waveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Nonreciprocal effect of transverse-magnetized ferromagnetic-metal-on-amplifier magnetooptical waveguides was numerically studied using the finite-difference beam-propagation method. It was shown that these waveguides can be used to obtain a monolithically integrated optical isolator. A detailed description and analysis of such an integrable isolator with better than 25 dB isolation ratio and low insertion loss in the 1.5 /spl mu/m wavelength region is given.

articleTitle: Geometric phase for the far zone field emitted by an open rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The article introduces Berry's (1984) geometric phase (GP) for the radiation field of an open rectangular waveguide for the first time. The decomposition of the total phase of the radiation field into a dynamical and a geometrical part is presented. The causes and characteristic features of GP are discussed.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of strip dipole antenna on stratified substrate
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper describes a generalization of the thin wire antenna integral equation for a curved strip dipole antenna on a stratified substrate. On the basis of the equivalent parameters method the equivalence of the models of a strip dipole antenna on plane layers and an insulated tubular antenna in an axially symmetric stratified medium is demonstrated. The approximation of transmission line theory results in formulas for the characteristic impedance of the strip dipole antenna on the stratified substrate and reveals the sinusoidal character of the current distribution function. The examined structure dispersion equation is also derived and solved.

articleTitle: Regularization of Maxwell equations, corner singularities and approximation
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe different formulations for the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves, with special emphasis on the consequences of the choice of the formulation on the finite elements discretization. Despite the fact that any solution of the problem is divergence-free, one must take account explicitly of this condition, for the associated operator is not strongly elliptic. Roughly speaking, one may handle this constraint either by duality or by penalty. Actually, the special form of Maxwell's equations makes the Lagrange multiplier a priori known, and the solution independent of the penalization coefficient. Another particular feature of the problem comes from the low regularity of the electromagnetic field in the vicinity of edges and conical points, from which it follows that special care must be taken of the choice of the function space for the penalty method.

articleTitle: On an application of iterative method of circular ferrite-dielectric waveguide analysis
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A tendency of growth of the differential phase shift /spl Delta//spl beta/, produced by a circular waveguide, filled with azimuthally magnetized ferrite has previously been established in the case where the outer part of the anisotropic medium is replaced by an isotropic dielectric toroid whose permittivity /spl epsiv//sub d/ exceeds that of the ferrite /spl epsiv//sub r/. The aim of this study is to specify the limits which /spl Delta//spl beta/ may reach, if the /spl epsiv//sub d///spl epsiv//sub r/-ratio gets very large. The boundary-value problem approach, extended with an iterative procedure, is applied, giving the phase characteristics of the structure.

articleTitle: Asymptotic radiation field of asymmetric planar dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In the spectral domain analysis of practical open integrated waveguiding structures, multiple non-removable branch points occur in the axial Fourier-transform plane. When the inversion integral for the distant radiation field is approximated asymptotically by deforming the real-axis integration contour (C) into a steepest-descent contour (SDC) all of the associated branch cuts are crossed twice. Passage from the top Riemann sheet to lower sheets and back to the top sheet occurs so both ends of the contour lie on the top sheet and C can be directly connected into SDC. If the observation aspect angle is sufficiently large, however, all but one of the cuts are crossed a third time and the two ends of the SDC lie on different sheets. Deformation of C into SDC then requires a fourth crossing of those cuts and integration around them to remain on the top sheet. A continuous spectrum contribution consequently augments the saddle-point term contributed by the SDC approximation. These wave phenomena are studied in detail for the asymmetric planar dielectric waveguide, which is the simplest canonical structure for which multiple non-removable branch points occur.

articleTitle: Beam propagation method for simulation of performance of vertical cavity surface emitting lasers
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In the design of modern optic fiber lines, telecommunications and information centers there is a problem of lasing sources with a wide modulation bandwidth, super small size, high efficiency and small threshold current. In many cases 2-D laser arrays are necessary. As a key element of laser arrays the vertical cavity lasers are used. In this work, the dependence of the threshold current on the output aperture for AlGaAs/GaAs and InGaAs/GaAs vertical cavity lasers with an implanted layer is investigated. For a description of the field distribution in various layers, the scalar Helmholtz equation in cylindrical coordinates is solved in view of the circular symmetry of the fundamental mode.

articleTitle: Time domain solution for the natural sub-ionospheric ELF pulse
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We model numerically the sub-ionospheric propagation of an electromagnetic wave in the extremely low frequency (ELF) band from a few hertz to several kilohertz using the time domain presentation for the field. A point vertical electric dipole is the source of the radio wave that arrives at the ground based observer through the spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity. We suppose the radiation moment of the source to be the delta-pulse, hence, the solution obtained is the Green's function of the problem. A formal representation for such a function is well-known either for the cases of postulated propagation constant or for a given effective surface impedance of the lower ionosphere. The formal solution is constructed using the zonal harmonic series representation (ZHSR) that applies Legendre polynomials describing the angular field dependence and spherical Hankel functions accounting for the radial dependence.

articleTitle: Nonlinear effects of the optical gain in the quantum well laser diodes
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The basic equations for modeling the dynamic characteristics of semiconductor lasers are the rate equations. One of their main parameters is the gain, which is defined by the optical gain coefficient. The linear form of this coefficient describes correctly the real behaviour of the laser under small pumping currents, however as the present research has shown, for a large electron density the gain is saturated and the dependence becomes nonlinear and that should be taken into account in the dynamic model. To determine the acceptable form of the gain in the set of the rate equations, we carry out an analysis of the carrier density influence on the optical gain taking into account the carriers density influence on the quasi-Fermi-level for the conduction and valence bands. We consider the differences in characteristics of lasers with bulk and quantum well (QW) active layers. The original function of the total density of the state dependence on the energy for QW lasers is proposed and used to reduce the computation time.

articleTitle: Guided-mode extracted integral equations for accurate CAD of dielectric branching waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In this paper, we present an accurate and computational-efficient BEM based on integral equations called guided-mode extracted integral equations (GMEIEs) for CAD of dielectric branching waveguide circuits. The advantage of this BEM is that it is possible to solve the problem without using mode-expansion techniques of open waveguide structures. So the method is very suitable for use in CAD of dielectric waveguide circuits. As an example a two dimensional branching waveguide is considered.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of an antenna with corner reflector
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The scattering of a field with known amplitude and phase distributions by a corner dielectric reflector is solved. To solve the problem, the Green's function method has been used. The formulas that characterize the fields in various cross sections that are suitable for numerical analysis have been obtained. The problem solution enables one to carry out the investigation of the dielectric structure reflection properties when the field of the original source has arbitrary amplitude and phase distributions. The total radiated field in the studied domain has been derived in the explicit form taking into account the polarization transform effect.

articleTitle: Analysis of the scattered field from the grating of resistive dipoles
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Microwire gratings may be used as a component of absorbing structures, so it is important to study different gratings consisting of resistive materials. Scattering of electromagnetic waves from a two-dimensional regular grating is investigated. The microwires are coated with a glass sheath. It has little effect on the electromagnetic properties but may have a much greater effect on the process of heat exchange in strong electromagnetic fields. A simulation methodology with reference of to the different parameters of the gratings is developed. Also, the degree of microwire heating is estimated for different intensities of the incident field.

articleTitle: Waveguide and anomalous properties of circular disk periodic chain embedded in 3D space
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Anomalous and waveguide properties of a periodic chain of circular disks are studied. The existence of waveguide and anomalous properties are proved to be independent of the chain period and the disk size. Classification of the waveguide modes according to the symmetry groups of problem are given. The number of waveguide modes and the dependence of waveguide frequencies on the geometric parameters is investigated.

articleTitle: A simple method inverting light-scattering data of a diffusive system into the particle size distribution function
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The information content of data for the spectral attenuation /spl sigma/ at /spl lambda/=0.55 /spl mu/m and for the Angstrom parameter /spl alpha/ in the visible range for the marine atmosphere was examined for the use in the reconstruction of the aerosol particle size spectrum. The particle size distribution curve was parameterized by a sum of two log-normal distributions, which means that it contained six unknown parameters to be determined from the two measured characteristics. Some parameters were fixed at their typical values in order to diminish the uncertainty of the problem. In the example illustrating the procedure, the total particle concentration and the fraction of the fine and large component were fixed. The number of members of the ensemble was great, because the answer was ambiguous. It is remarkable, however, that in the active particle interval, different members of the ensemble have close distribution curves, so it is natural to accept an average curve as a solution to the problem. In spite of the small body of initial information, the accuracy of the procedure was quite reasonable. It can also be seen how the error grows with the particle radius.

articleTitle: Resonance properties of Bragg structures with parameter distortion
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)

articleTitle: Impact of variations in the radioactive background above the Earth on the ionization balance in the lower ionosphere
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A lithosphere-ionosphere interaction model is put forward, involving atmospheric vertical conduction electric currents, the variations of which can change the electric potential of the lower ionosphere. The ionospheric parameter variations have been estimated, compared with the gathered data, and both quantitative and qualitative agreement found.

articleTitle: Method of investigation of linear polarization of intensive laser radiation
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The author considers a method of measuring the angle of the direction of linear polarization of intensive and wide-aperture laser radiation by three bolometric grids having a non-linear transformation character. This method is explained. It essentially decreases the systematic errors of the measurements, removes non-registrable angle regions, and is an evolution of the measurement method proposed by Kuzmichov and Kuzmichova (1996).

articleTitle: Remote sensing by VLF using "Absolute OmniPAL". 1. Investigation of the decay of sprite plasma
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We consider observations by Dowden et al. (1997) of very strong early/fast Trimpis or VLF sprites observed at Darwin, Australia, only 2,000 km from the US Navy transmitter, NWC (21/spl deg/48'S, 114/spl deg/9'E). The unperturbed signal strength was about 20 mV/m during the Trimpi observations (at night). The echo amplitudes of the strong Trimpis ranged up to 8 mV/m, some 30 dB stronger than those studied previously in Colorado. The much higher signal/noise ratio enabled accurate measurements of the time variation of the amplitude and phase of the echoes.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of whispering gallery mode coupler in dielectric slab waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Coupling of the 2D complex source point (CSP) beam into a dielectric slab waveguide using a circular cylindrical dielectric resonator is studied. Sample numerical results and coupling efficiency are presented. It is shown that the maximum value of the coupling efficiency depends on the beamwidth and illuminating angle as well as on the frequency.

articleTitle: Computer simulation in antenna design and measurements
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The fulfilment of the requirements for the reduction of the development time and implementation of modern antennas, the increase in productivity of the engineers, optimization of antennas performance, and high accuracy and completeness of measurements of their characteristics requires special automated imitating-measuring complexes (AIMC), which enable one to integrate the processes of designing, modeling, aligning and testing of antennas. AIMC should consist of a simulation modeling system (SMS) and an automated measuring system (AMS). The SMS is used at all the antenna development stages, from design to acceptance testing.

articleTitle: Boundary equations in the problems of electromagnetic wave diffraction on 3-D unclosed surfaces
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: This investigation continues the research previously carried out by the authors which were devoted to the diffraction problems on closed surfaces. In these papers the unique solvability of various systems of non-stationary boundary equations was proved in some functional spaces of the Sobolev type. In this paper they consider the problem of electromagnetic wave diffraction on an unclosed surface /spl Gamma//sub 0/ in R/sup 3/ which models an ideal conductor.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering by rectangular-cell double-periodic magneto-dielectric gratings
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic waves scattering by a double-periodic grating is solved by the new method based on the rigorous volume integro-differential equations. The Galerkin method is applied to reduce this volume integro-differential equation to set of second-order differential ones with constant coefficients in functionals. Numerical solution was obtained for the simplest double-periodic magneto-dielectric rectangular-cell grating as an example of a structure with translational symmetry.

articleTitle: Classification of wave instabilities produced by interaction of grating modes
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We present the criteria and the main results of the wave instability studies in a phase grating containing space harmonic set. It is now generally accepted that all instabilities may be reduced to those of Bragg's kind. The Bragg's correlations pertain, however, only to the special case periodical system. The existence of instabilities is due to interaction between electromagnetic wave and phase grating modes. The periodicity of the grating is likely to be unimportant. By combining our analytical studies with model calculations may lead to a better understanding of wave instabilities.

articleTitle: Eigen-value electrodynamic problems for IR carbon nanowaveguides
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper considers guided wave propagation in carbon nanotubes. For finding the impedance boundary condition we calculate surface axial conductivity in the semiclassical approach based on the Hamilton function given in the tight-binding model. The dependence of the wavenumber of the surface eigenwave versus its frequency is found numerically accounting for attenuation.

articleTitle: Galerkin methods in solving integral equations with applications to scattering problems
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The Galerkin methods of obtaining approximate solutions of integral equations and their applications to problems of scattering of electromagnetic and surface water waves are examined. Two typical problems, one occurring in electromagnetic wave propagation and the other in the propagation of two dimensional surface water waves, are taken up as illustrative examples of the methods.

articleTitle: Structure of the local Alfven resonance in cylindrical plasmas placed into rippled magnetic field
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Conditions are determined under which axial modulation of the steady magnetic field affects significantly the structure of the local Alfven resonance (AR) in quasi-cylindrical plasma fusion devices. The behaviour of the Alfven wave (AW) electromagnetic fields within the AR region is studied utilizing the perturbation theory and "narrow slab" approach.

articleTitle: The cost of pleasure: about some catastrophes in time-harmonic wave scattering
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper is concerned with a review of several situations taking place in the time-harmonic wave scattering (/spl sim/e/sup -i/spl omega/t/) when solutions to certain wave scattering problems do not exist. Each of these situations is closely tied to the violation of solution uniqueness, due to a presence of an eigenvalue, in terms of either natural frequency or propagation constant, simple or multiple, coinciding with the corresponding parameter of the excitation field. Then the reason of solution non-existence call be easily understood. From the physical point of view, the mentioned catastrophes are always a result of joint action of several major assumptions, such as harmonic time-dependence, absence of losses or nonlinearities, and infinite extension of the scatterer. Thus, a loss of solution existence, at certain discrete values of parameters, is the cost of the pleasure of working with a simplified problem.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic spectra of magnetics with spontaneously broken spin symmetry and B-phase of Fermi-superfluid
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: In the present paper, we consider the theory, describing both spiral magnetics and superfluid Fermi-liquid with a triplet pairing. Previously this method was used in the description of a superfluid Fermi-liquid in the singlet case. This approach is a generalization of the classical theory of Fermi-liquid. This semiphenomenological study combines the advantages of both the microscopic and phenomenological description. The method permits the spectra of collective excitations of the system to be obtained taking into account the Fermi-liquid effects.

articleTitle: Diffuse photon probes of dynamic nonhomogeneities in random high scattering media
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: We have measured non-invasively the liquid flow changes by using a photon correlation spectroscopy with a simple correlation diffusion model for studying and monitoring the dynamic nonhomogeneities in a random high scattering media. The method utilizes the Doppler broadening of light that arises in a multiply scattering dynamic medium, and is also responsive to changes in the absorption and scattering coefficients. Our measurements clearly show the flow changes that qualitatively agree with the theory.

articleTitle: Radiation of a long conductor excited by a short pulse
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A great number of papers devoted to the investigation of nonstationary radiation of wire antennas were published, but most of them have a theoretical character. In the well-known experimental works the electromagnetic field was radiated and registered near a metal surface. To use ultrawideband (UWB) impulse signals in practice, it is required to radiate and receive signals in free space. The study of peculiarities of UWB impulse signal radiation and reception was carried out taking as an example a long conductor disposed perpendicularly to a metal plate, the most simple arrangement for investigation.

articleTitle: Universal method of calculation of optimal parameters of bipolar electromagnets
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A general method of design of geometric sizes and electrical parameters of bipolar electromagnets is given. The basis of the method is a joint mathematical modelling of electromagnetic and thermal processes.

articleTitle: On radar images modelling of structures with complex microgeometry
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The problem of radar images modelling has become a hot topic in connection with remote sensing technique enhancements. This paper is devoted to a research by means of a computation experiment of those new qualities which surface microgeometry brings into radar image properties. The size of microgeometry does not exceed the wavelength /spl lambda/. The problem of H-polarized plane wave scattering from perfectly conducting smooth and rough cylindrical surfaces was considered by means of the method of discrete singularities (MDS). One-dimensional radar images h(r) were computed and discussed.

articleTitle: Scattering and absorption of a videopulse by a set of alternated layers with resistive films
