publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper deals with videopulse reflection from a periodic layered structure with resistive films. The role of resistive films under the videopulse-structure interaction is described. The influence of the number of periodic composite cells is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the dispersion characteristics of shielded microstrip line
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A modified method of the Riemann-Hilbert problem is proposed for analyzing guided waves in a shielded microstrip line (MSL). In this paper the method is illustrated by an example, namely the analysis of the dispersion characteristics of a microstrip line. The dispersion characteristics for the microstrip line are computed over a wide frequency band including the resonance region.

articleTitle: Recent developments in fast-multipole based frequency and time domain solvers
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: This paper reviews the state of the art in fast integral equation techniques for solving large scale electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems. The multilevel fast multipole algorithm and its frequency and time domain derivatives are discussed. These techniques permit the rapid evaluation of fields due to known sources and hence accelerate the solution of boundary value problems arising in the analysis of a wide variety of electromagnetic phenomena. Specifically, the application of the steepest descent fast multipole method to the frequency domain analysis of radiation from quasi planar structures, e.g., rough surfaces and finite microstrip structures, is described. In addition, the extension of the fast multipole concept to the plane wave time domain algorithm that permits the efficient analysis of transient phenomena is outlined.

articleTitle: Low frequency scattering of a plane wave by an anisotropic ellipsoid in anisotropic medium
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The Newtonian potential method has been applied to calculate the scattering of a plane wave from an anisotropic dielectric ellipsoid in anisotropic medium. It should be noted that the results of the present paper are applicable to wave scattering by a collection of anisotropic particles.

articleTitle: Microwave method for the step-like reconstruction of lossless multilayered dielectrics
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: A novel one-dimensional microwave imaging approach based on successive reconstruction of dielectric interfaces using the complex reflection coefficient data collected over some standard waveguide band is described. The method is valid for highly contrasted discontinuous profiles and shows low sensitivity to the practical measurement error. Some numerical examples are presented.

articleTitle: TE-wave scattering by a multiangular trough in a conducting plane
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering of a transverse electric wave by an infinite loaded trough of a multiangular cross-section is studied using the domain product technique which employs a Mathieu function expansion. The algorithm gives the possibility of a substantial variation of the geometry of the trough without turning to another mathematical model. Numerical examples are presented which demonstrate the validity and capability of the technique.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering by dielectric cylinder half-immersed in the perfectly conducting half-space
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: To investigate the features of various media by means of electromagnetic radiation, it is necessary to know the field scattered by the nonhomogeneities of this media. This problem can be solved with sufficient accuracy and adequacy by using, as a basis, a rigorous solution of the basic model (Nefedov 1979). One of the basic models for this purpose can be the considered structure. The aims of this paper are to investigate the scattering of a plane wave by a circular dielectric cylinder (CDC), half immersed in the perfectly conducting half-space; the method of re-expanding in terms of the basis functions at the given interval is used (Smimov 1957; Shepilko 1979). Applying the boundary condition to the Fourier-Bessel series representation of the scattered field, our problem is reduced to the solution of a matrix equation for unknown expansion coefficients. These coefficients are determined numerically with high accuracy after truncation of the matrix equation. The scattered field is evaluated asymptotically and the backscattering radar cross section (BRCS) expression is derived. Accurate numerical results are presented for the E- and H-polarized waves.

articleTitle: Low-frequency asymptotics in the diffraction of waves by echelette
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of the problem of H-polarized plane wave diffraction from a symmetrical metallic echelette whose dimensions are small comparing to the wavelength. To solve the problem, we apply the quasistatic Green function method.

articleTitle: Interference of acoustic waves in solid layer with periodically irregular boundary
publicationTitle: MMET Conference Proceedings. 1998 International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. MMET 98 (Cat. No.98EX114)
abstract: The investigation of the acoustic guided wave propagation continues to be a topical problem of the bounded medium wave theory due to a wide range of applications of acoustic devices. There has been a great number of papers devoted to the study of wave propagation along irregular surfaces. Since the waveguides of various geometries are employed in the design of acoustic, and microwave systems, many similar problems have been analysed in detail by computational methods for the specific applications. Nevertheless, the physical phenomena, which can be described by analytical solutions, have not been revealed in a full manner, at least in some cases. We present a theoretical analysis of the transverse acoustic wave propagation in an isotropic solid layer with free boundaries, one of which has one-dimensional periodically irregular shape.
